title: A cursor move in neovim selects the node it lands on, even inside the selection
body:
Since 29eef0c a cursor message selects the innermost node holding the cursor, except that a cursor inside an already selected node changes nothing. Two effects Jack found: with a stack selected, moving the cursor into one of its boxes keeps the stack selected; and a cursor in the indentation before a nested box selects the stack, because that whitespace lies in the stack's span but not the box's.

## Proposal

- Drop the inside-selection rule. The viewer remembers the offset of the last `goto` it sent and ignores one cursor message at exactly that offset (the echo); every other cursor message selects the innermost node, so a box selection still survives the echo of its own `goto`.
- A cursor in the leading indentation of a line counts as on the line's first non-blank character. Blank lines between children and a container's own lines still select the container.
close_reason: Landed in cbc9c02. `Selection::at_cursor` in `crates/acre-gui/src/selection.rs` no longer takes the old selection, and maps the offset through `on_line` (indentation to the line's first non-blank byte, trailing blanks to its last). `App::goto` in `app.rs` holds the last goto's offset and ignores one cursor at that offset in the next batch.
